ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC on every direct shareholder, UBO and proposed director: PEP identification per Article L. 561-10-2 CMF including family members and close associates; 4-eyes approval for PEP relationships under Article L. 561-15 CMF; systematic screening of all persons and project-cargo counter-parties against the consolidated UN Sanctions Lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions (Regulations (EU) 269/2011 and 2580/2001), the French asset-freeze list (sanctions.gouv.fr / gels d'avoirs), and OFAC sanctions where USD clearing or any US nexus is present in Milestone_Wire or Letter_of_Credit payment rails; dual-use and controlled-item screening under Council Regulation (EU) No. 428/2009 and the French Code de la défense is applied to OOG heavy-haul freight. Standard corporate intelligence is sufficient; no PEP-red-flag triggers are expected for this Low_Risk_Standard ISIC 5229 project-cargo logistics structure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle), feeding the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) — public search via data.inpi.fr and commercial extracts via Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be expressed in Latin-script characters capable of French phonetic rendering; French law does not require a name composed of French words, but the legal entity element must appear in the name, either in full as 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or as the initials 'SAS'; registered corporate names and INPI/EUIPO trademarks take priority in identity control; Cyrillic, Arabic or Asian-script UBO and shareholder names require sworn French transliteration at filing accompanied by certified translator certification
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Caisse / Crédit (reserved to regulated credit institutions under the Monetary and Financial Code L. 511-1)
Assurance / Réassurance (reserved under the Insurance Code L. 310-1)
Pharmacie / Officine (reserved under the Public Health Code L. 4211-1)
Avocat / Notaire / Huissier de justice / Expert-comptable (reserved to licensed liberal-profession title-holders)
France / République / Nationale / Ministère (suggesting French State sponsorship or public authority affiliation)
Port / Gare / Aéroport (implying a public facility concession or infrastructure operator status when none exists)
Union / Fédération (misleading reference to union or professional-body standing in a manner contravenant à l'ordre public)
Transport Exceptionnel / Magazine? (terms suggesting regulated public-passenger transport or media licensing where no appropriate operational permit exists)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a statutory de jure name-reservation certificate. Identity control is performed at incorporation filing by INPI/RNE, comparing the requested name against the RNE, INPI trademark database, and existing trade signs; a passing preliminary search gives a de facto 30-day pre-filing hold before the formal incorporation is transmitted. Upon rejection, the incorporator must obtain the written formal refusal notification from the Guichet Unique/INPI; counsel shall file a reasoned administrative recourse (procédure gracieuse) before the President of the competent commercial court (Tribunal de Commerce or the commerce chamber of the Tribunal Judiciaire) within 15 days from receipt of the refusal, attaching a re-run clearance search on revised name variants; in parallel, a corrected name may be re-filed immediately through the Guichet Unique. If the administrative recourse is denied, judicial remedy is available by voie de référé before the same commercial court within one month from notification of the denial, and final correction may also be sought after incorporation through a modification of the RNE entry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this non-licensed services industry via an approved commercial domiciliation provider under Article L. 123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code. The registered seat (siège social) must remain a fixed French address to which legal and tax supervision is attributed; the domiciliation contract must be in writing and recorded at the RNE. For freight-arrangement operations, banks and shippers may nevertheless require a substantive office where bills of lading, heavy-haul route permits, customs files and contracts of carriage can be administratively serviced.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified on-site inspection risk is approximately 10% during the first fiscal year: unannounced visits are infrequent for unregulated ISIC 5229 services but may occur tangentially through DREAL/DDT customs-compliance checks on OOG heavy-haul documentation, URSSAF payroll controls, and tax-administration audits addressing intra-EU VAT on cross-border project-cargo invoicing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), acting through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Corporate income tax and VAT administration is conducted through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal. VAT numbers for French-established entities are allocated by the DGFiP. Non-established EU and non-EU businesses generally register through the competent French VAT service for foreign businesses or appoint a French tax representative where legally required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate and register the SAS with the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). 2. Obtain the SIREN and SIRET identifiers and the applicable activity classification from the national business register. 3. Open the professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr using the legal representative's or authorized agent's credentials. 4. Submit the required tax registration information, including legal name, registered office, business activities, accounting period, bank details, establishment information, and expected VAT transactions. 5. Request VAT registration from the competent SIE where the SAS conducts taxable activities. 6. Receive the French VAT identification number in the format FR plus a two-digit key and the nine-digit SIREN. 7. For intra-Community transactions, validate counterparties' VAT numbers through the EU VIES system and maintain transaction evidence. A foreign entity without a French establishment must register before undertaking French VAT-taxable transactions when no applicable simplification or reverse-charge rule removes its registration obligation. A non-EU entity generally requires a French fiscal representative unless a specific legal or treaty-based exemption applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. An SAS meeting statutory conditions may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu), generally for a maximum of five financial years, subject to conditions concerning ownership, employee headcount, turnover or balance-sheet size, unlisted status, business activity, and individual ownership of capital and voting rights. The election is not a general United States-style check-the-box election. No general French hybrid-mismatch election changes the entity's legal classification. Anti-hybrid mismatch provisions may deny deductions or impose inclusion where arrangements produce deduction/non-inclusion or duplicate deduction outcomes. French tax residence generally follows the place of effective management or the location of the registered office, subject to applicable tax treaties. A non-resident entity is taxed on French-source profits or profits attributable to a French permanent establishment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), governed principally by the French Tax Code and the EU VAT Directive framework
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France has no universal VAT registration threshold for a business that is required to charge French VAT. Small-business franchise en base thresholds may apply instead. For services, including many logistics services, the principal annual turnover threshold is EUR 37,500, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 under the applicable rules. For deliveries of goods and comparable activities, the principal threshold is EUR 85,000, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500. A business exceeding the relevant threshold or otherwise losing the franchise must register and charge VAT from the legally prescribed date. Foreign businesses may have a French VAT registration obligation from their first taxable French transaction, irrespective of the domestic small-business threshold, unless reverse charge, an exemption, or another simplification applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved private platforms (plateformes agréées), with the French public invoicing portal serving as the state platform framework. All French-established businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuing obligations are scheduled to apply from 1 September 2026 to large and medium-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 to small and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory implementation changes. Domestic B2B invoices will generally be transmitted through an approved platform, and specified B2C and cross-border transactions will be reported through e-reporting. France does not operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance requirement for all transactions. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. There is no universal statutory digital stamp requirement for ordinary commercial invoices, but invoices must contain mandatory VAT particulars, be issued and retained in an auditable form, and satisfy authenticity, integrity, and legibility requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT when the supplier establishes that the goods physically leave the EU and satisfies the French customs and documentary requirements. The supplier must retain the export declaration and customs evidence of exit, normally including the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and an electronic exit result or equivalent proof. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt from French VAT where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched or transported to that Member State, and the supplier retains the required transport and VAT-number evidence. For services, France generally applies place-of-supply rules rather than a technically defined zero-rate. B2B services supplied to a business established outside France are generally located at the customer's establishment and are invoiced without French VAT where the conditions are met. B2B services supplied to an EU business are generally subject to the customer's Member State reverse charge. Logistics, freight-forwarding, and heavy-haul services require transaction-specific analysis, particularly where services are connected with imports, exports, immovable property, passenger transport, or intermediary services. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, business purpose, non-exempt taxable activity, and compliance with applicable deduction restrictions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
French or EU customs export declaration
Electronic customs exit confirmation or other legally accepted proof that the goods exited the European Union
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, CMR consignment note, or equivalent multimodal transport record
Evidence linking the commercial invoice, export declaration, goods, and transport movement
Import or destination-country customs documentation where available
Customer VAT identification evidence for intra-Community supplies, where applicable
Proof of payment or bank records where relevant to evidencing the transaction; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a statutory condition for export VAT exemption
Contracts, purchase orders, freight instructions, delivery records, and subcontractor records supporting the actual supply and export chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export VAT treatment. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to banking, anti-money-laundering, accounting, sanctions, and transfer-pricing requirements. If export exemption or an input VAT refund is unsupported, the DGFiP may reassess output VAT, deny or claw back input VAT, charge late-payment interest, and impose tax penalties. Common penalties include a 10% surcharge for specified late or non-compliant filings, a 40% surcharge for deliberate failure, and an 80% surcharge for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Late-payment interest is generally charged at the statutory rate applicable for the relevant period. Customs authorities may apply Union Customs Code recovery, administrative penalties, seizure, or other customs measures for false declarations or unsupported export status. Serious intentional tax fraud may also trigger criminal proceedings, including imprisonment and substantial fines. Export documentation must therefore be retained for the applicable French accounting and tax limitation periods, commonly at least six years for tax audit purposes, with longer retention where another legal obligation applies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank. France has no separate general foreign-exchange administration imposing routine exchange controls. Applicable oversight also includes the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution), the French Financial Markets Authority (Autorité des marchés financiers), the French Customs Directorate for applicable reporting, and the French anti-money-laundering authority Tracfin.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions within the applicable European Union framework. A French SAS may generally receive, hold, convert, and remit euros and foreign currencies without a general licensing requirement, mandatory use of a domestic bank, capital controls, or profit-repatriation approval. Dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, shareholder-loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds may be remitted subject to distributable-profit rules, corporate approvals, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing requirements, treaty entitlement, beneficial-owner verification, anti-money-laundering controls, sanctions screening, and proof of the underlying transaction. Banks may require invoices, contracts, board resolutions, tax forms, source-of-funds evidence, and ultimate-beneficial-owner information before execution. Foreign direct investment screening may apply to investments in protected strategic sectors; ordinary project-cargo logistics is generally outside the protected-sector perimeter unless the transaction involves a protected asset, technology, infrastructure, or activity. Cash payments and certain cross-border cash movements remain subject to anti-money-laundering and customs restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for an exporter to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's discretion, subject to bank controls, accounting in euros, tax compliance, sanctions compliance, and contractual financing covenants. Trade, customs, VAT, statistical, and balance-of-payments information may be collected through customs declarations, banking records, Intrastat or successor EU reporting systems, and Banque de France statistical reporting where applicable. Any cash carried across an external European Union border at or above the applicable declaration threshold must be declared to customs. The company should document invoice currency, receipt date, settlement currency, hedge designation, exchange rates, and reconciliation to customs and accounting records.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for routine EUR collections, SEPA payments, expense management, and selected foreign-currency services; Medium or Low as the sole treasury bank for capital injections, high-value project-cargo settlements, documentary credits, guarantees, cash deposits, and complex trade finance. A licensed electronic-money institution or payment institution in France or another European Economic Area state may provide services under its authorization and passporting framework, but it does not provide bank deposits unless separately licensed as a credit institution. Customer funds must be safeguarded rather than treated as ordinary insured bank deposits, and services remain subject to payment-services law, safeguarding rules, transaction limits, sanctions screening, AML/KYC, source-of-funds controls, and provider risk appetite. Offshore digital EMIs without an applicable European authorization or lawful passport should not be used for regulated payment services directed at France. Maintain a regulated French or EEA bank as the primary account for shareholder funding, tax payments, payroll, trade finance, and liquidity concentration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal rule requiring every director to appear physically at a bank branch to open an SAS account. Remote onboarding may be accepted where the bank can complete reliable identity verification, beneficial-ownership verification, management verification, tax-residence certification, and source-of-funds assessment. Banks may nevertheless require a video interview, certified or apostilled corporate documents, notarized identification, a French or EEA contact address, a local signatory, or an in-person meeting under their risk-based policies. A newly incorporated SAS may need a temporary capital-injection account before registration and conversion to a permanent operational account after receipt of the Kbis extract and registered articles. Non-resident shareholders and directors are legally permitted, but non-resident ownership commonly increases documentary and enhanced-due-diligence requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered ultimate-beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, bearer-equivalent arrangements, or inconsistent ownership information across corporate records and bank forms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; Kbis extract; shareholder register; organizational chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and residential-address evidence for directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners; ownership declarations; certified translations where requested; and written explanation of any holding-company chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder funding, large capital injection, or shareholder loan with no clear economic rationale or source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement or shareholder-loan agreement; board or shareholder resolutions; proof of originating account ownership; audited financial statements or management accounts of the funding entity; bank statements; sale, financing, or dividend documentation establishing source of funds; tax-residence certificates; and a transaction-flow memorandum linking the funds to the SAS business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Project-cargo payments involving high-value machinery, unusual routing, multiple intermediaries, sanctioned jurisdictions, or counterparties with limited public information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer and supplier master files; signed logistics, freight-forwarding, chartering, and transport contracts; purchase orders; commercial invoices; bills of lading or transport documents; customs declarations; end-use and end-user statements; sanctions-screening results; beneficial-owner checks for counterparties; route and vessel information; and an escalation protocol for restricted-party or diversion risks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash-intensive settlement, unexplained third-party payments, circular transfers, or funds received from an unrelated group company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved payment-policy manual; intercompany agreements; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; third-party-payment authorization; bank statements; accounting ledger extracts; beneficial-owner relationship evidence; written commercial rationale; and prohibition of personal-account or unapproved cash settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between stated activity, ISIC classification, projected turnover, account geography, and actual transaction profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; customer and corridor matrix; expected monthly transaction volumes; currencies; average ticket size; countries of operation; fleet, warehouse, and subcontractor information; regulatory and customs registrations; insurance certificates; sample contracts; and a 12-month cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed person exposure, corruption concerns, tax-residence inconsistency, or sanctions and export-control risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and sanctions-screening records; compliance certifications; tax-residence forms; tax identification numbers; anti-bribery and sanctions policies; litigation and adverse-media explanation; independent legal opinions where appropriate; and enhanced-approval records from the company's compliance officer or board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for documentary credits, guarantees, or high-value international transfers without adequate collateral, credit history, or transaction documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bankable financial statements; borrowing-base or collateral schedule; insurance and credit-insurance evidence; confirmed purchase and sale contracts; documentary-credit application; pro forma invoices; transport and customs documents; counterparty credit information; authorized signatory matrix; and documented transaction-risk controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through the SAS capital-injection account opened with a regulated French credit institution or eligible EEA institution, using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding or SWIFT cross-border payment messaging for non-SEPA currencies. The remitter name must match the subscriber or documented group funding entity, and the payment reference should identify the legal basis, such as share subscription, share-premium contribution, or shareholder loan. There is no universal French foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary corporate transfers; the bank may nevertheless require an internal payment purpose, LEI, tax information, source-of-funds evidence, and supporting contracts. For equity, provide the subscription decision, articles, capital amount, share-premium terms, and depositary instructions. After incorporation or capital increase, obtain the deposit certificate and reconcile the bank credit to the registered capital and share premium. For shareholder loans, provide the executed loan agreement, maturity, interest, transfer-pricing support, withholding-tax analysis, and any applicable French related-party reporting. For all wires, validate IBAN, BIC, beneficiary legal name, intermediary-bank details, sanctions status, and payment repair procedures. Reconcile incoming funds to the general ledger and retain bank confirmations, FX rates, and supporting documents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within applicable scheme limits and bank availability; use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or successor ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or international payments. Use documentary commercial letters of credit, preferably subject to UCP 600, for higher-risk equipment, cross-border procurement, milestone-based project cargo, or counterparties requiring bank-backed payment. Consider confirmed, transferable, standby, or deferred-payment structures only after reviewing fees, collateral, tenor, governing law, sanctions exposure, and documentary discrepancies. Payment files should include invoice number, contract or purchase-order reference, goods or service description, currency, amount, transport documents, customs data where relevant, and beneficiary verification. Apply segregation of duties, dual authorization, callback controls for payment-detail changes, sanctions screening at initiation and release, and three-way reconciliation among contract, invoice, and delivery evidence. Retain MT103 or ISO 20022 confirmation, LC application and amendments, presented documents, discrepancy notices, bank charges, and settlement records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for forecast or contracted receipts and payments, subject to bank credit limits, documented hedging purpose, counterparty onboarding, and appropriate accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or limited delivery markets, subject to the bank's product availability, settlement mechanics, sanctions controls, EMIR and MiFID-related obligations, and documented commercial exposure.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and currency maturity matching, subject to master documentation, collateral terms, counterparty limits, and treasury-policy approval.
Currency options and collars for asymmetric project-cargo cash-flow exposure, subject to suitability, pricing, premium, accounting, and governance controls.

Cross-currency swaps for longer-term funding or structural currency exposure, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral and valuation terms, EMIR reporting or clearing analysis, and board-approved risk limits.

Hedging must be limited to identifiable commercial, financing, or liquidity exposures and must not constitute unauthorized speculative dealing. The SAS should maintain a treasury policy covering permitted instruments, approved counterparties, tenor limits, hedge ratios, valuation, collateral, close-out rights, accounting designation, confirmation matching, and independent controls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; no regulatory filing at the approval stage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court-authorized extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A shareholder may seek a court order compelling the president to convene the meeting; failure to prepare or submit accounts may also result in criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual accounts and related documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe) for filing in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval if filed in paper form, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The registry or an interested party may seek a court injunction, potentially with a daily penalty. Failure to deposit accounts may be punishable by a fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat offenses. No automatic strike-off period applies solely for late accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year company, generally the second working day after 1 May, subject to the annually published electronic-filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increasing in specified circumstances, plus late-payment interest; penalties may also apply for inaccuracies or omissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner information update, if reportable information changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry maintaining the Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after a change in beneficial-owner information; no routine annual confirmation is required if information remains unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate or timely beneficial-owner information may trigger criminal fines and, for responsible individuals, possible imprisonment; no automatic strike-off timeline applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Separate requirements may apply to groups, controlled entities, or regulated activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French commercial accounting rules and the French General Chart of Accounts (Plan comptable général). IFRS is generally not mandatory for an unlisted SAS's individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no routine annual UBO confirmation. File an update with the commercial court registry within 30 days after any change in beneficial-owner identity, control, or relevant particulars. Record share transfers in the company's securities movement register and update the relevant shareholder accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share movements and individual securities accounts
Minutes and written decisions of shareholders
Accounting records and supporting documents, retained in accordance with applicable French requirements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 500–2,000 annually, depending on provider and services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000–10,000 annually for a small SAS; not applicable unless an auditor is required or appointed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A reduced 15% rate may apply to qualifying small and medium-sized companies on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory ownership, turnover and paid-in-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying new businesses may access regional or activity-based exemptions, including certain qualifying start-up, priority-area and research-related regimes. Research and development tax credits may generally be available at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure incurred in France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to qualifying conditions and documentation. The reduced SME rate applies only where all statutory conditions are met. France does not generally provide a blanket corporate tax holiday for ordinary project-cargo logistics activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, filed electronically with the corporate tax package through the French tax administration portal impots.gouv.fr using the EDI-TDFC or EFI electronic channel. The package normally includes forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD and the relevant balance-sheet, income-statement and tax reconciliation schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for the corporate income tax return; quarterly instalment payments are generally required during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and tax package are generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second business day following 1 May, subject to the deadline displayed by the French tax administration. Corporate tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The final balance is generally due by the statutory balance-payment deadline following filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, principal activity, fiscal year dates, tax office and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS must report its French legal identity and SIREN number. A non-resident shareholder, parent or counterparty is not substituted for the French SAS as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, tax regime and group status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability, applicable tax regime, tax consolidation status and filing method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the ordinary French corporate tax regime unless a valid tax-consolidated group election or special regime applies. A non-resident parent does not itself create French tax consolidation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-A-SD, accounting profit to taxable income reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation differences, provisions, financial expenses, foreign taxes and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only items attributable to the French SAS. Foreign-head-office costs or related-party charges must be supported by benefit evidence, allocation keys and arm's-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, prior-year losses carried forward, losses utilized and losses remaining available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses legally attributable to the French entity. French loss utilization is subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year profit exceeding EUR 1 million, with additional rules for changes in activity or ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-C-SD, tax credits and tax reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, foreign tax credits where applicable and amounts carried forward or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits must comply with the relevant tax treaty and French limitation rules. A foreign tax payment is not automatically creditable merely because it was withheld.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, tax balance sheet and capital information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax balance sheet, provisions, depreciation, capital gains, shareholding information and movements affecting taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intercompany equity, debt, fixed assets and capital transactions consistently with the statutory accounts and related-party documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation and payment of each corporate tax instalment and applicable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS pays instalments based on prior-year or estimated current-year liability. A newly incorporated company may have no instalment obligation until the first statutory payment cycle, subject to current-year liability and applicable thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax liability, instalments paid, credits, balance payable or overpayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to the 2065-SD return and bank payment. Do not net shareholder-level withholding tax against the SAS corporate tax balance unless legally permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Request for refund or allocation of corporate tax credits or overpayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the French bank account and supporting evidence. Refund entitlement remains subject to validation of the underlying tax credit and return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information supporting cross-border related-party transactions, transfer-pricing adjustments, financing, royalties, management fees and guarantees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the foreign legal entity, jurisdiction, transaction type, amount, pricing method and contractual basis. Apply French documentation and reporting rules where statutory thresholds are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed corporate tax returns may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% in specified formal notice situations and potentially 80% in cases of fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, subject to statutory adjustments and exceptions. Inaccurate returns may trigger tax reassessment, interest, tax penalties and, in serious cases, criminal tax-fraud proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD for corporate tax instalments and Form 2572-SD for the final corporate tax balance, filed electronically through impots.gouv.fr or the authorized EDI channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalments, with an annual final balance statement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The fourth instalment and final balance may be subject to special percentage and deadline rules depending on the company's prior-year corporate tax liability and applicable large-company provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of the current instalment based on prior-year corporate tax or estimated current-year liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate using the French entity's own taxable results. Foreign parent tax payments do not reduce the French SAS instalment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible tax credits applied against the instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only credits legally available to the French SAS and retain evidence of eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability less instalments, credits and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all amounts to the filed annual return, general ledger, bank evidence and tax account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late instalments or final balances may generate 0.20% monthly late-payment interest and a 5% surcharge for late payment in applicable cases. Deliberate underpayment or inaccurate tax-credit claims may result in additional penalties, reassessment and criminal exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The standard French withholding tax on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident beneficiary is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, domestic exemptions and anti-abuse conditions. The French SAS must generally file and pay the withholding using the applicable withholding tax forms and procedures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its home-country tax authority and the applicable French treaty-relief forms, commonly Forms 5000-FR and 5001-FR for dividends, interest or royalties, as relevant. Relief at source requires documentation acceptable to the French payer and tax administration; otherwise the statutory amount may be withheld and the recipient may seek a refund. Treaty relief normally requires beneficial ownership, treaty residence, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse compliance where applicable, and satisfaction of the treaty's participation and holding-period conditions. The EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption generally requires qualifying EU or EEA ownership, a minimum participation threshold and holding-period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to a non-resident may be subject to domestic withholding, generally at a rate aligned with the applicable French corporate tax rate, currently 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption. Certain royalties paid to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions may face a 75% rate. Ordinary outbound interest paid by a French company is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, but special rules may apply for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, profit-participating instruments, disguised distributions or specific regulated instruments. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 15% and interest withholding to 0% to 10%, but the exact rate depends on the applicable treaty, beneficial ownership and anti-abuse requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory full transfer-pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or where it is owned, directly or indirectly, by an entity meeting that threshold, or where it belongs to a qualifying group meeting the statutory conditions. A French entity below the threshold must still apply the arm's-length principle and be able to substantiate its pricing. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Annual simplified transfer-pricing declarations may apply to entities meeting separate statutory thresholds, commonly including EUR 50 million turnover or gross assets or a qualifying group relationship.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime applicable generally to ordinary French SAS companies. Nevertheless, French tax law applies substance-over-form principles, the abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, anti-hybrid rules, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules and general anti-abuse provisions. The SAS should maintain French operational substance proportionate to its logistics activity, including genuine management, personnel or outsourced operational control, premises or facilities where appropriate, customer and supplier contracts, decision-making records, bank activity, transport documentation and commercially justified related-party arrangements. A passive conduit or contractual intermediary without corresponding functions, assets and risks is high risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.transfer_pricing_operational_requirement: Intercompany freight coordination, brokerage, management services, financing, guarantees, insurance support, software, trademarks and procurement must be priced by reference to functions performed, assets used and risks assumed. The file should contain the group structure, business description, functional analysis, tested party, method selection, comparable search, benchmarking, intercompany agreements, financial data and reconciliation to statutory accounts. A year-end true-up should be supported by contemporaneous documentation and should not be used to manufacture losses or shift routine logistics profits to a low-tax jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing project-cargo revenue, issuing false invoices, suppressing freight income, fabricating expenses, claiming fictitious input VAT, diverting customer receipts or intentionally misrepresenting taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, 40% or 80% tax penalties depending on the conduct, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions that may include up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, increased in aggravated cases to up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, confiscation, director disqualification and civil tax-liability proceedings where they organized or materially contributed to fraudulent non-payment. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from judicial control, criminal proceedings or enforcement measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using fictitious subcontractors, reclaiming VAT without genuine transport or logistics services, participating in missing-trader chains, issuing invoices without supply, or misclassifying domestic and cross-border freight.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, recovery of improperly deducted or refunded VAT, late-payment interest, 40% or 80% penalties, potential joint and several liability in specified fraud circumstances, and criminal fraud sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may incur criminal liability for knowingly participating in VAT fraud and may face personal asset exposure where serious and repeated tax misconduct supports a judicial tax-liability claim.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive management fees, royalties or interest; assigning French logistics functions to a foreign entity without substance; guaranteeing related-party debt without remuneration; or setting prices that systematically eliminate French taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to arm's-length profit, interest, tax penalties, documentation penalties and possible withholding-tax reassessment. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation can result in a specific penalty, potentially up to 0.5% of the amount of transactions lacking documentation or 5% of the reassessed profits, subject to statutory limits and the applicable calculation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and, where intentional fraud is proven, criminal consequences for directing artificial profit shifting. Normal commercial losses do not create personal liability if pricing is commercially supported and properly documented.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, conduit or abuse-of-law arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SAS with no real decision-making, personnel, commercial risk or operational purpose while routing profits, dividends, royalties or financing through it solely to obtain tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic tax benefits, recharacterization of transactions, corporate tax and withholding-tax reassessment, abuse-of-law penalties that may reach 80% in aggravated cases, and possible criminal investigation where false documents or fraud are involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for knowingly implementing an artificial arrangement, including civil restitution, management bans, confiscation and criminal penalties. A travel ban is possible only if ordered under applicable judicial or enforcement procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable reserves, paying dividends while net equity is below statutory limits, disguising shareholder withdrawals as expenses, or making non-arm's-length payments to shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unlawful distributions, corporate and shareholder tax reassessment, withholding tax, penalties, director liability and potential insolvency-related claims. Certain unlawful distributions may constitute criminal corporate-officer misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable to restore improperly distributed amounts and may face civil damages, management disqualification and criminal sanctions where the distribution was knowingly unlawful.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained milestone wires, opaque beneficial ownership, high-risk third-country payments, unusual letters of credit, cash structuring, false invoices or transactions inconsistent with the customer's logistics profile without appropriate due diligence or escalation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal money laundering may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with higher sanctions for aggravated or organized conduct. Corporate sanctions, confiscation and regulatory consequences may also apply. Reporting failures by regulated professionals can trigger supervisory sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate laundering may face imprisonment, personal fines, confiscation and management restrictions. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a criminal court or investigative judge but are not an automatic consequence of an AML deficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file or update the beneficial-owner register, concealing the ultimate shareholder, using nominees to obscure control, or submitting inaccurate corporate-registration information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court orders, fines, registration restrictions and criminal penalties may apply for failure to disclose or inaccurate disclosure. The company may face enhanced scrutiny by banks, tax authorities and customs authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative may be personally prosecuted for knowingly false or incomplete filings and may face fines, management disqualification and, where linked to fraud, confiscation or imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: False customs valuation, origin or classification for oversized industrial cargo; evasion of duties; prohibited routing; sanctions evasion; handling controlled goods without required authorization; or falsifying transport and customs records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Seizure, forfeiture, customs recovery, administrative fines, suspension or loss of customs authorizations, and criminal sanctions for serious customs or sanctions offenses. Penalties depend on the goods, conduct, jurisdiction and applicable EU and French measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible managers may be prosecuted where they ordered, approved or knowingly tolerated the breach. Courts may impose fines, confiscation, professional bans and, in serious cases, imprisonment or travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False accounting, forged documents and obstruction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining off-book accounts, fabricating bills of lading, transport certificates or supplier invoices, destroying accounting records, obstructing a tax audit or refusing legally required information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting and corporate-law penalties, evidentiary presumptions against the company, criminal sanctions for forgery or obstruction, and possible confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, accounting officers and de facto managers may incur personal criminal liability, civil damages, disqualification, confiscation and judicial travel restrictions where ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using undeclared drivers or workers, misclassifying employees as independent contractors, failing to verify subcontractor compliance, or arranging labor through fictitious service companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Social-security reassessment, surcharges, administrative fines, exclusion from public contracts, joint liability in specified cases and criminal sanctions for concealed work.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability and personal civil exposure where they knowingly organized concealed work or ignored obvious subcontractor irregularities. Management bans and confiscation may apply in serious cases.
